specialties.name: Cardiology & Cardiac Surgery
specialties.description: Interventional cardiology and cardiac surgery: angioplasty, bypass (CABG), valve repair and replacement, TAVI, pacemakers and congenital heart repair by high-volume heart teams.

specialties.name: Orthopedics & Joint Replacement
specialties.description: Knee, hip and shoulder replacement, sports injuries and arthroscopy with computer-navigated and robotic-assisted options and in-hospital physiotherapy.

specialties.name: Cosmetic & Plastic Surgery
specialties.description: Aesthetic and reconstructive procedures such as rhinoplasty, liposuction, tummy tuck, breast surgery and hair restoration by board-certified plastic surgeons.

specialties.name: Dental Care
specialties.description: Implants, full-mouth rehabilitation, root canal treatment, crowns and veneers planned with 3D scans; many treatments fit into a one- or two-week trip.

specialties.name: Oncology (Cancer Care)
specialties.description: Multidisciplinary cancer care: tumour-board review, chemotherapy and immunotherapy, precision radiotherapy, radiosurgery and cancer surgery.

specialties.name: Neurology & Neurosurgery
specialties.description: Brain and nerve care including brain tumour surgery, aneurysm treatment, epilepsy surgery and deep brain stimulation for movement disorders.

specialties.name: Fertility & IVF
specialties.description: IUI, IVF, ICSI and fertility preservation delivered under India's Assisted Reproductive Technology regulations, with counselling throughout.

specialties.name: Organ & Bone Marrow Transplant
specialties.description: Living-donor liver and kidney transplants and bone marrow transplants. Organ transplants for international patients require a related donor and approval under Indian transplant law.

specialties.name: Bariatric & Weight-Loss Surgery
specialties.description: Sleeve gastrectomy, gastric bypass and non-surgical balloon options with dietitian and psychologist support before and after surgery.

specialties.name: Ophthalmology (Eye Care)
specialties.description: Laser vision correction, premium cataract surgery, corneal transplant and retina surgery, mostly as day-care procedures.

specialties.name: Spine Surgery
specialties.description: Minimally invasive and open spine surgery: slipped disc, spinal fusion, artificial disc replacement and scoliosis correction with neuro-monitoring.

specialties.name: Urology
specialties.description: Kidney stone removal, prostate enlargement surgery and robotic cancer surgery using laser and endoscopic techniques.

specialties.name: Gastroenterology & GI Surgery
specialties.description: Keyhole gallbladder, hernia and colorectal surgery plus advanced endoscopy for digestive and liver conditions.

specialties.name: ENT (Ear, Nose & Throat)
specialties.description: Cochlear implants, endoscopic sinus surgery, tonsillectomy and thyroid surgery for adults and children.

specialties.name: Nephrology & Dialysis
specialties.description: Kidney care for international patients: haemodialysis while in India, dialysis access surgery and transplant work-up.

specialties.name: Wellness & Preventive Health
specialties.description: Comprehensive health check-ups and supervised Ayurveda and lifestyle programmes alongside conventional medical oversight.

procedures.name: Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG)
procedures.description: Open-heart surgery that reroutes blood around blocked coronary arteries using grafts from the chest wall, leg or arm. Performed on- or off-pump, followed by about a week in hospital and supervised cardiac rehabilitation.

procedures.name: Coronary Angioplasty with Stenting (PTCA)
procedures.description: Minimally invasive procedure that opens narrowed coronary arteries with a balloon and a drug-eluting stent through a small puncture in the wrist or groin. Most patients go home within two days.

procedures.name: Heart Valve Replacement / Repair
procedures.description: Surgical repair or replacement of a damaged aortic or mitral valve with a mechanical or tissue valve, including minimally invasive approaches where suitable.

procedures.name: Pacemaker Implantation
procedures.description: Implantation of a single- or dual-chamber pacemaker for slow or irregular heart rhythms, under local anaesthesia with a short hospital stay.

procedures.name: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI)
procedures.description: Catheter-based replacement of a narrowed aortic valve without open-heart surgery, suited to older or higher-risk patients.

procedures.name: Congenital Heart Defect Repair (ASD/VSD)
procedures.description: Device closure or surgical repair of holes in the heart (ASD/VSD) and other congenital defects in children and adults by paediatric cardiac teams.

procedures.name: Total Knee Replacement (TKR)
procedures.description: Replacement of a worn knee joint with a durable implant using conventional, computer-navigated or robotic-assisted techniques. Most patients walk with support the day after surgery.

procedures.name: Bilateral Knee Replacement
procedures.description: Both knees replaced in one admission (same day or staged a few days apart), reducing the total recovery time and cost for arthritis in both knees.

procedures.name: Total Hip Replacement (THR)
procedures.description: Replacement of a damaged hip joint with a ceramic or polyethylene-bearing implant to relieve pain and restore mobility.

procedures.name: ACL Reconstruction
procedures.description: Arthroscopic (keyhole) reconstruction of a torn anterior cruciate ligament with a tendon graft, followed by a structured rehabilitation programme.

procedures.name: Shoulder Replacement
procedures.description: Anatomic or reverse total shoulder replacement for severe arthritis, complex fractures or irreparable rotator cuff tears.

procedures.name: Knee Arthroscopy (Meniscus Repair)
procedures.description: Keyhole surgery to repair or trim a torn meniscus, remove loose bodies or treat cartilage damage, usually as a day-care or overnight procedure.

procedures.name: Spinal Fusion Surgery
procedures.description: Stabilisation of unstable or slipped vertebrae with screws, rods and bone graft, increasingly with minimally invasive techniques.

procedures.name: Artificial Disc Replacement
procedures.description: Replacement of a degenerated cervical or lumbar disc with a motion-preserving artificial disc as an alternative to fusion.

procedures.name: Microdiscectomy (Slipped Disc Surgery)
procedures.description: Minimally invasive removal of a herniated disc fragment pressing on a nerve, relieving sciatica or arm pain.

procedures.name: Scoliosis Correction Surgery
procedures.description: Surgical correction of abnormal spinal curvature with instrumentation and continuous neuro-monitoring, for adolescents and adults.

procedures.name: Chemotherapy (per cycle)
procedures.description: Day-care chemotherapy, targeted therapy or immunotherapy given per protocol by a medical oncology team. Priced per cycle; high-cost biologics are quoted separately.

procedures.name: Radiation Therapy (IMRT/IGRT course)
procedures.description: A course of precision radiotherapy planned on CT/MRI and delivered over several weeks as an outpatient.

procedures.name: Breast Cancer Surgery
procedures.description: Breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy with sentinel node biopsy, with options for oncoplastic reconstruction.

procedures.name: Stereotactic Radiosurgery (SRS/SBRT)
procedures.description: High-precision, high-dose radiation in one to five sessions for brain tumours, metastases and selected body tumours, without incisions.

procedures.name: Whipple Procedure (Pancreaticoduodenectomy)
procedures.description: Complex surgery for tumours of the pancreatic head, bile duct or duodenum, performed by high-volume hepato-pancreato-biliary teams.

procedures.name: Liver Transplant (Living Donor)
procedures.description: Living-donor liver transplantation for end-stage liver disease or liver cancer. International patients need a related donor and approval from the hospital authorisation committee.

procedures.name: Kidney Transplant (Living Donor)
procedures.description: Living-donor kidney transplantation, including ABO-incompatible options, with donor evaluation and authorisation committee approval as required by Indian law.

procedures.name: Bone Marrow Transplant (BMT)
procedures.description: Autologous, matched or haplo-identical stem cell transplant for leukaemia, lymphoma, myeloma, thalassaemia and aplastic anaemia in HEPA-filtered transplant units.

procedures.name: Brain Tumour Surgery (Craniotomy)
procedures.description: Removal of brain tumours with neuronavigation, intra-operative monitoring and, where appropriate, awake craniotomy.

procedures.name: Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS)
procedures.description: Implantation of brain electrodes and a neurostimulator to control symptoms of Parkinson's disease, dystonia and essential tremor.

procedures.name: Epilepsy Surgery
procedures.description: Comprehensive evaluation (video-EEG, MRI, PET) followed by surgery to remove or disconnect the seizure focus in drug-resistant epilepsy.

procedures.name: Brain Aneurysm Coiling / Clipping
procedures.description: Endovascular coiling or surgical clipping of brain aneurysms to prevent or treat bleeding.

procedures.name: IVF (In Vitro Fertilisation) Cycle
procedures.description: One complete IVF cycle: ovarian stimulation, egg retrieval under sedation, fertilisation, embryo culture and transfer, in line with India's ART regulations.

procedures.name: ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection)
procedures.description: IVF with direct injection of a single sperm into each egg, recommended for male-factor infertility or previous fertilisation failure.

procedures.name: IUI (Intrauterine Insemination)
procedures.description: Placement of prepared sperm into the uterus around ovulation; a simple first-line fertility treatment.

procedures.name: Egg Freezing (Oocyte Cryopreservation)
procedures.description: Stimulation, retrieval and vitrification of eggs to preserve fertility for medical or personal reasons.

procedures.name: Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy
procedures.description: Keyhole weight-loss surgery that removes about three-quarters of the stomach, reducing appetite; often improves type 2 diabetes and blood pressure.

procedures.name: Gastric Bypass (Roux-en-Y)
procedures.description: Laparoscopic bypass that creates a small stomach pouch connected to the small intestine; effective for severe obesity and metabolic disease.

procedures.name: Intragastric Balloon
procedures.description: Endoscopic placement of a temporary saline-filled balloon in the stomach for 6-12 months as a non-surgical weight-loss option.

procedures.name: LASIK Laser Vision Correction (both eyes)
procedures.description: Bladeless laser correction of short-sightedness, long-sightedness and astigmatism; most patients resume normal activities within one or two days.

procedures.name: Cataract Surgery (Phaco with Premium Lens, per eye)
procedures.description: Micro-incision phacoemulsification with a monofocal, toric or multifocal intraocular lens, usually under local anaesthesia as a day-care procedure.

procedures.name: Corneal Transplant (Keratoplasty)
procedures.description: Full-thickness or partial (DMEK/DSAEK) corneal transplantation for corneal scarring, keratoconus or endothelial failure.

procedures.name: Retinal Detachment Surgery / Vitrectomy
procedures.description: Vitreo-retinal surgery to repair retinal detachment, clear vitreous haemorrhage or treat macular holes and diabetic eye disease.

procedures.name: Rhinoplasty (Nose Reshaping)
procedures.description: Open or closed reshaping of the nose for aesthetic or breathing reasons, often combined with septoplasty.

procedures.name: Hair Transplant (FUE, about 3,000 grafts)
procedures.description: Follicular unit extraction (FUE) hair restoration under local anaesthesia over one or two days.

procedures.name: Liposuction (Body Contouring)
procedures.description: Removal of stubborn fat from areas such as the abdomen, flanks, thighs and arms using tumescent or power-assisted techniques.

procedures.name: Abdominoplasty (Tummy Tuck)
procedures.description: Removal of excess abdominal skin and fat with tightening of the abdominal muscles, often after pregnancy or major weight loss.

procedures.name: Breast Augmentation
procedures.description: Breast enlargement or reshaping with implants or fat transfer, performed by qualified plastic surgeons.

procedures.name: Dental Implant with Crown (per tooth)
procedures.description: Titanium implant with abutment and zirconia or porcelain crown; immediate-loading options can keep your stay to about a week.

procedures.name: Full-Mouth Rehabilitation (Implant-Supported)
procedures.description: Restoration of all teeth with implant-supported fixed bridges for one or both jaws, planned with 3D scans and digital smile design.

procedures.name: Root Canal Treatment with Crown
procedures.description: Single- or two-sitting root canal therapy followed by a ceramic crown to save an infected or damaged tooth.

procedures.name: Porcelain Veneers (per tooth)
procedures.description: Thin ceramic shells bonded to the front of teeth to improve colour, shape and alignment as part of a smile makeover.

procedures.name: Robotic Radical Prostatectomy
procedures.description: Robot-assisted removal of the prostate for localised prostate cancer, with smaller incisions, less blood loss and faster recovery.

procedures.name: Prostate Enlargement Surgery (TURP / HoLEP)
procedures.description: Endoscopic removal of excess prostate tissue (TURP or holmium laser HoLEP) to relieve urinary symptoms of benign prostatic enlargement.

procedures.name: Kidney Stone Removal (RIRS / PCNL)
procedures.description: Laser stone removal through the urinary tract (RIRS) or a keyhole puncture (PCNL), chosen by stone size and position.

procedures.name: Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy (Gallbladder Removal)
procedures.description: Keyhole removal of the gallbladder for gallstones or inflammation, usually with a one-night stay.

procedures.name: Laparoscopic Hernia Repair
procedures.description: Keyhole repair of inguinal, umbilical or incisional hernias with mesh reinforcement.

procedures.name: Laparoscopic Colorectal Surgery
procedures.description: Minimally invasive surgery of the colon and rectum for cancer, diverticular disease or inflammatory bowel disease.

procedures.name: Cochlear Implant (one ear)
procedures.description: Implantation of a cochlear implant for severe-to-profound hearing loss in children and adults, followed by device activation and mapping sessions.

procedures.name: Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery (FESS)
procedures.description: Endoscopic surgery to clear blocked sinuses and nasal polyps, often combined with septoplasty.

procedures.name: Tonsillectomy
procedures.description: Removal of the tonsils (with or without adenoids) for recurrent infections or sleep-disordered breathing, using coblation or conventional techniques.

procedures.name: Thyroidectomy
procedures.description: Partial or total removal of the thyroid gland for nodules, goitre, hyperthyroidism or thyroid cancer, with nerve monitoring.

procedures.name: Haemodialysis (4-week course, 12 sessions)
procedures.description: Maintenance haemodialysis three times a week for kidney failure, including for patients awaiting transplant evaluation in India.

procedures.name: AV Fistula Creation for Dialysis
procedures.description: Surgical creation of an arteriovenous fistula in the arm to provide long-term access for haemodialysis.

procedures.name: Executive Health Check-up
procedures.description: A comprehensive one-day preventive assessment: blood tests, cardiac screening (ECG, echo, stress test), imaging and specialist consultations.

procedures.name: Ayurveda Panchakarma Programme (14 days)
procedures.description: A supervised 14-day classical Ayurveda detox and rejuvenation programme with daily therapies, diet and yoga, alongside conventional medical oversight.

cultural_tips.title: Namaste: greeting people in India
cultural_tips.body: A warm 'Namaste' with palms pressed together works everywhere and is always polite. Handshakes are common in hospitals and business settings; some people prefer not to shake hands with the opposite gender, so let them lead. Using titles such as 'Doctor', 'Sir' or 'Madam' is appreciated.

cultural_tips.title: Dining etiquette and food safety
cultural_tips.body: Many Indians eat with the right hand; cutlery is always available in hotels and hospitals. Vegetarian food is widely available, and halal, Jain and other diets can be arranged. Drink sealed bottled or filtered water, choose freshly cooked hot food, and follow any diet your care team gives you.

cultural_tips.title: What to wear
cultural_tips.body: Light, breathable cotton clothing suits most of the year. Modest dress (covered shoulders and knees) is respectful at temples, mosques and gurudwaras, where you will also remove your shoes. Pack a light jacket for air-conditioned hospitals and for North India in December and January.

cultural_tips.title: Tipping
cultural_tips.body: Tipping is appreciated but never mandatory. In restaurants, 5-10% is customary if no service charge is included; small tips for porters, drivers and hotel staff are common. Hospital staff should not be tipped - use the hospital's feedback form to thank your care team instead.

cultural_tips.title: Festivals and public holidays
cultural_tips.body: India celebrates many festivals, such as Diwali (October/November), Holi (March), Eid and Christmas. Hospitals stay open, but some outpatient clinics close and traffic, crowds and fireworks increase. Your coordinator will plan appointments around local holidays.

cultural_tips.title: Staying safe and comfortable
cultural_tips.body: Keep your passport and visa copies in your phone and with your coordinator, and the originals in the hotel safe. Use registered taxis or app-based cabs, especially at night. Save the 24x7 helpline and dial 112 for police, fire or ambulance emergencies anywhere in India.

cultural_tips.title: Getting a local SIM card
cultural_tips.body: International visitors can buy a prepaid SIM at airport counters or official stores with their passport, visa and a passport photo; activation can take a few hours. eSIMs and international roaming also work. Hospital Wi-Fi is usually available for messaging and video calls.

cultural_tips.title: Money and payments
cultural_tips.body: The currency is the Indian Rupee (INR, ₹). Cards are accepted at hospitals, hotels and larger shops; carry some cash for small purchases and auto-rickshaws. Exchange money only at banks or authorised dealers and keep the receipts. QR-code (UPI) payments are everywhere - ask your coordinator about options available to international visitors.

cultural_tips.title: Getting around
cultural_tips.body: App-based cabs are the easiest way to travel in big cities, and many have metro rail too. Agree the fare before taking an auto-rickshaw without a meter. Traffic can be heavy, so allow extra time for hospital appointments; your package may include local transport.

cultural_tips.title: Hospital etiquette
cultural_tips.body: Carry your passport, visa and previous reports to every appointment. Hospitals usually allow one attendant with a visitor pass, and visiting hours are limited in ICUs and wards. Keep noise low, follow infection-control rules and ask your international patient desk for an interpreter at any time.
